messages.subject: Re: estitmator= MLMV vs MLMVS
messages.body_plain:
On 02/28/2013 02:46 PM, Nj�l Foldnes wrote:
> The mean and variance adjusted chi-square as proposed by Satorra and
> Bentler is now available as MLMVS, if I understand this correctly?

Yes.

> What is the difference between MLMV and MLMVS? The MLMV does not seem to
> adjust the df.

Good question. MLMV and MLMVS are two different approaches to 'adjust'
the chi-square test statistic (and/or its degrees to freedom), to better
approximate the chi-square distribution.

Estimator="MLMV" and estimator="MLMVS" is short for

- estimator="ML"
- se="robust"
- test="mean.var.adjusted" (MLMVS, with S for Satterthwaite)
or
- test="scaled.shifted" (MLMV)

test="mean.var.adjusted" is the familiar 'Satterthwaite' approach
(adjusting both the mean and the variance), and is well documented in
the literature. One reference is:

Satorra, A., & Bentler, EM. (1994). Corrections to test statistics and
standard enors in covariance structure analysis. In A. von Eye & C.C.
Clogg (Eds.), Latent variables analysis: Applications for developmental
research (pp. 399-419). Thousand Oaks, CA: Sage.

available here:
http://www.econ.upf.edu/~satorra/CourseSEMVienna2010/SatorraBentler1994.pdf
(see eqs 16.23 and 16.24)

Now, for many years, estimator MLMV in Mplus referred to this
Satterthwaite correction. With the 'MV' standing for 'mean' and
'variance' adjusted. But from Mplus 6 onwards, they changed this, and
the *MV extension (in MLMV, ULSMV, WLSMV) is now by default referring to
a 'scaled-shifted' correction, documented here:

https://www.statmodel.com/download/WLSMV_new_chi21.pdf

Very, very few users noticed this. And the *MV extension is not helping
(it should be MLSS, for scale+shift). Note that apart of this web note,
there is no published paper about this (AFAIK).

In Mplus 6 and higher, it is still possible to request the Satterthwaite
version, but then you need to add an option 'Satterthwaite=on' somewhere.

In lavaan, the *MV extension refers to the scaled-shifted correction (as
in Mplus 6 and higher). The *MVS extension refers to the Satterthwaite
correction.

These estimator types are for Mplus users, and they should result in
identical results. Non-Mplus users are perhaps better off using the
'test' argument directly.

> BTW: ULS offers the MV option, but not the MVS option, is there some
> particular reason for that?

That is an oversight on my part. Both ULMVS and WLSMVS are now added to
the dev version (0.5-12).

Yves.

It's probably better to use the data in its natural metric for input and then in the summary() or parameterEstimates() function, use the standardized=TRUE argument to get fully standardized (i.e, latent and observed variables) results. They will be in the std.all column.

As far as standardized results being preferable, that is not always the case. As with regression, it depends on your variables and what questions you are wanting to answer. Typically, it's good to examine unstandardized, standardized and (if applicable) structure coefficients.

Alex

if you don't care about the natural metric, you could standardise your data, e.g.
using

In plant ecology you might deal with non-normal count data a lot? Count data can be handled (without transforms) by Mplus, I think lavaan doesn't do that (for now..?)

> The difference in chi-squared values for nested models estimated with

True, but lavaan uses a 'scaled' difference test, using the (correct)
formulas from Satorra (2000). (reference below).

> In his syntax examples of the book "Confirmatory Factor Analysis for
> Applied Research", Jan Lammertyn pointed out that the difference test
> was not yet implemented in lavaan for categorical variables.

It is now. Note that the results reported in Brown are based on an older
version of Mplus. To get identical results for the two model fits, you
can use estimator="WLSMVS" (with S for Satterthwaite) and mimic="Mplus".
The latter will round-off the fractional degrees of freedom to integers.

> In the book, using Mplus, it is reported:
>
> Chi-Square Test for Difference Testing Value 27.958 Degrees of Freedom
> 4** P-Value 0.0000

Well, if estimator="WLSMVS" and mimic="Mplus" is used, anova(fit1 ,fit2)
gives

 > anova(fit1, fit2)
Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (test = mean.var.adjusted)

      Df AIC BIC   Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit1  9          5.6512

fit2 13         42.1617     26.199  3.7111  2.077e-05 ***

Still not the 27.958 repored by Mplus, and note the fractional degrees
of freedom. lavaan is using Satorra (2000). Mplus is using a slightly
different approach (described in webnote 10 on the Mplus website).
AFAIK, both approaches are correct (and one day, I will add a
mimic="Mplus" to the anova() function too to get the exact Mplus result).

Yves.

Satorra, A. (2000). Scaled and adjusted restricted tests in multi-sample
analysis of moment structures. In Innovations in Multivariate
Statistical Analysis: A Festschrift for Heinz Neudecker. Heijmans,

You should avoid ADF/WLS (unless you have a huge sample size, say
N>5000). MLR and bootstrapping work equally well. For some subtle
differences, see

Yuan, KH & Hayashi K (2006). Standard errors in covariance structure
models: Asymptotics versus bootstrap. British Journal of Mathematical
and Statistical Psychology, Vol. 59, No. 2. (November 2006), pp.
397-417, doi:10.1348/000711005x85896

Bootstrapping, of course, takes (much) more time.

Yves.

messages.body_plain:
hello yves and fellow lavaan users!

to begin with, i would like to thank everyone who is involved in the lavaan project. for poor graduate students like myself with not enough money to spend on software like Mplus or EQS having access to it has been a true blessing.

i am trying to teach myself a little more "advanced" SEM techniques (latent mediation/moderation, multilevel sem, finite mixture models, etc.) through easy simulations and was just wondering...  how does lavaan calculate the standard error of the indirect and total effects in a mediation with latent variables? is it through the delta method as well? i am using the following (very simple) code to simulate data and fit my model. if there are any mistakes i would appreciate the input :-)

model1 <-

     '#measurement model

     X =~ 0.5*y1 + 0.5*y2 + 0.5*y3
     M =~ 0.7*y4 + 0.7*y5 + 0.7*y6
     Y =~ 0.9*y7 + 0.9*y8 + 0.9*y9

     #direct effect
     Y =~ 0.75*X

     #mediator
     M =~ 0.75*X
     Y =~ 0.75*M

     #variances

     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
     Y~~1*Y'

datum <- simulateData(model1, model.type=sem, sample.nobs=5000)

fitz <-

     '#measurement model
     X =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3
     M =~ NA*y4 + y5 + y6
     Y =~ NA*y7 + y8 + y9

     #direct effect
     Y =~ a*X

     #mediator
     M =~ b*X
     Y =~ c*M

     #indirect effect
      ab:= a*b

    #total effect
      total:= c + (a*b)

     #variances
     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
      Y~~1*Y'

summary(sem(fitz, data=datum, mimic="Mplus"))

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to sem and have been having difficulty trying to fit models with more that one composite variable in them. I do not know whether this is a problem with model specification (i.e. I'm not doing it right and am having mathematical troubles) or a problem with lavaan's fitting of the model.

In my most basic model I am trying to model the effect of six climatic variables on one response- lichen richness. Two variables, wetness and mat exhibit a unimodal relationship with this variable, so I am attempting to account for this non-linearity using two composite variables, each of which includes a linear and squared term of the climate variable.

This full model will not fit:

clim_mod = '

# Non-linear terms
optimal_wetness <~ 1*wetness + wetness2
wetness ~~ wetness2

optimal_mat <~ 1*mat + mat2
mat ~~ mat2

# Regressions
lichen.rich_log ~ optimal_wetness + optimal_mat + pseas + iso + rain_lowRH
'
clim_fit = sem(clim_mod, data=working_data, meanstructure=T, fixed.x=FALSE)

But the models with only one composite in them will fit:

clim_mod1 = '

# Non-linear terms

wetness ~~ wetness2

# Regressions

'

clim_mod2 = '

# Non-linear terms
optimal_mat <~ 1*mat + mat2
mat ~~ mat2

# Regressions
lichen.rich_log ~ wetness + optimal_mat + pseas + iso + rain_lowRH
'

I have also had other instances where models with more than one composite will not fit, but this is the most straightforward example. I have attached a relevant dataframe.

messages.subject: simsem and semTools updates
messages.body_plain:
Dear lavaan users,

The simsem and semTools packages have been updated on CRAN. Here are the updates from the previous version on CRAN:

[March 17, 2013] Latest Update: simsem, Version 0.5-3

This version is available on CRAN and KRAN. This simulation result of this version can save confidence interval computed by any methods (e.g., bootstrap or profile-likelihood). The coverage rate can be investigated by getCoverage, findCoverage, and plotCoverage functions. The confidence interval widths can be investigated by getCIwidth and plotCIwidth, which allows users to estimate sample size and percent missing for accuracy in parameter estimation. The inspect function is written to extract the information from the simulation result, such as inspect(Output, "fit") for fit indices of convergent replications. The summaryTime, summarySeed, and coef are also written to extract information from the simulation result. The empirical argument is added into the generate and createData functions to create multivariate normal data with the sample statistics equal to the model-implied means and covariance matrix from the provided parameters.

[March 9, 2013] Latest Update: simsem, Version 0.5-2

This version is available on KRAN. The major update in this function is that users can write a function that returns vectors of parameter estimates, standard errors, fit indices, and convergence status and specify it in the model argument in the sim function. See the help page of the sim function for an example. A minor bug in multiple group analysis was fixed.
[March 17, 2013] Latest Update: semTools, Version 0.3-2

This version is available in CRAN and KRAN. The wald function is added to conduct multivariate Wald test for any linear combinations of parameters. This function is equivalent to MODEL TEST feature in Mplus.
[February 15, 2013] Latest Update: semTools, Version 0.3-1

This version is available in KRAN only. The problem in the lisrel2lavaan function has been fixed.

Links

simsem: http://simsem.org/

semTools: https://github.com/simsem/semTools/wiki

Best,

Sunthud

Hello -

I'm conducting a CFA with 4 latent constructs, assuming they are correlated, with 22 manifest variables (between 4 and 7 per construct). All the manifest variables are dichotomous 0/1. I am running the cfa with an ordered statement, as follows:

facc_mod1a<-'
appm=~APPM004+APPM005+APPM011+APPM013+APPM014+APPM016+APPM019
apsp=~APSP003+APSP004+APSP005+APSP015
cpdcr=~CPDCR001+CPDCR002+CPDCR014+CPDCR017+CPDCR018
cpdr=~CPDR001+CPDR002+CPDR003+CPDR006+CPDR025+CPDR026
'

facc_mod1a.fit<-cfa(facc_mod1a,data=facc,ordered=c(
'APPM004','APPM005','APPM011','APPM013','APPM014','APPM016',
'APPM019','APSP003','APSP004','APSP005','APSP015','CPDCR001',
'CPDCR002','CPDCR014','CPDCR017','CPDCR018','CPDR001','CPDR002',
'CPDR003','CPDR006','CPDR025','CPDR026'
))

I get this warning message:
 lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite;. use inspect(fit,"cov.lv <http://cov.lv>") to investigate.

When I run the eigen function off of the inspect function, I indeed get the following eigenvalues:
1.08470493  0.07351025  0.02207286 -0.01323814

My question is, how can I address this in my model? I'm not 100% up on my matrix algebra these days - can I assume that the -0.013 is small enough to be considered non-negative? Can I somehow manually manipulate the eigenvalues to set the lowest equal to zero? If I could do so, would I want to? Part of my goal is to see if I can combine constructs, so if indeed there is a zero eigenvalue would that be evidence that one of the constructs is a linear combination of the others?

Thanks for any guidance,

Robin

messages.subject: Re: [simsem] generating predictions for fit models
messages.body_plain:
The simsem package needs the matrix format to generate data with covariates. The example is in the following link:

https://github.com/simsem/simsem/blob/master/SupportingDocs/Examples/Version05/exMultipleFormat/covData.R

However, we can get around the matrix specification by a little trick. I will show an example here:

library(simsem)
library(lavaan)

# Create MIMIC model with one factor
script <- "
f1 =~ 1*y1 + 1?y2 + 1?y3
f1 ~~ 0.75?f1
f1 ~ 0.5?x1
f1 ~ 0.5?x2
y1 ~~ 0.5?y1
y2 ~~ 0.5?y2
y3 ~~ 0.5?y3
"

# Use the cfa function to read the script without analyzing any data
template <- cfa(script, do.fit=FALSE, fixed.x=TRUE)

# Use model.lavaan function to transcribe the output of lavaan to simsem matrix format
template2 <- model.lavaan(template)

# Create covariate data. The number of rows must equal to the target sample size.
covData <- data.frame(x1 = rbinom(100, 1, 0.5), x2 = rpois(100, 4))

# To generate data with covariates, the covData argument is used to supply the exogenous covariates
dat <- generate(template2, n = 100, covData=covData)

# Try to analyze a single data set
out <- cfa(script, data = dat, fixed.x=TRUE)
summary(out)

# Run a simulation
simout <- sim(nRep = 20, n = 100, model = template2, covData=covData)
summary(simout)

I am not sure I answer all of your questions. Hopefully, this script will help you start your project. A good documentation on the exogenous covariates has not written yet. I will try to write it soon.

Sunthud
